AccessTokenDetail.description:
A personal access token's metadata; the value is never returned
again after creation.
AccessTokenDetail.title: AccessTokenDetail

AuthorOut.description:
Who published a version. ``username`` is null only if the account
cannot be found (users are disabled, never deleted).
AuthorOut.title: AuthorOut

CostReport.description: A list-price estimate, never billing data (see ``CostEstimate``).
CostReport.title: CostReport

DraftBody.description: The editable graph state. GET returns it; PUT sends it back whole.
DraftBody.title: DraftBody

DurationStats.description:
Over ``count`` samples. Percentiles are nearest-rank: always a
duration that was actually observed.
DurationStats.title: DurationStats

EventOut.description:
The stored event (architecture §18), payload redacted on the way out
like every output channel (observability §12).
EventOut.title: EventOut

EventPage.description:
Pass ``next_after`` as ``after`` to continue: the next page while
``has_more``, later events of a running execution otherwise.
EventPage.title: EventPage

ExecutionDetail.description:
The canonical execution representation: what every trigger returns
and what execution listings contain. Node-level detail is the report.
ExecutionDetail.title: ExecutionDetail

ExecutionListItem.description:
An execution in a listing: the canonical representation plus its
workflow's current name, joined in the same query. Single-execution
responses omit it; the public webhook response must not disclose it.
ExecutionListItem.title: ExecutionListItem

FailureReport.description:
A failed attempt of a node. ``attempt`` is derived, not stored: the
only way back to READY is ``retry``, which records the failure, so the
n-th recorded failure always ended attempt n (``NODE_ACTIONS``).
FailureReport.title: FailureReport

ImportWorkflowResponse.description:
The new workflow (an unpublished draft), its validation result and the
referenced credentials this installation does not have yet.
ImportWorkflowResponse.title: ImportWorkflowResponse

LogLevel.description: Python's level names; the order is severity (``at_least``).
LogLevel.title: LogLevel

LogLineOut.description:
A stored node log line. Redacted again on the way out, like events:
the runtime redacted it when it was captured, this guards older rows
against rules added since.
LogLineOut.title: LogLineOut

PositionBody.description: Editor canvas coordinates; layout only, ignored at runtime.
PositionBody.title: PositionBody

PublishWorkflowRequest.description: Optional: pin publishing to the revision the client validated.
PublishWorkflowRequest.title: PublishWorkflowRequest

RestoreVersionRequest.description: ``expected_revision`` is the draft revision being replaced.
RestoreVersionRequest.title: RestoreVersionRequest

Role.description:
ADMIN manages the installation (users, credentials, every workflow);
MEMBER works on the workflows they own.
Role.title: Role

StatusCounts.description: Every execution status with its count (zero included).
StatusCounts.title: StatusCounts

SystemStatus.description: /health and /ready for API clients: the UI reaches only /api/v1.
SystemStatus.title: SystemStatus

TimelineBucket.description:
Executions created in ``[start, end)``. The last bucket ends at
``until`` and may be shorter than ``bucket_seconds``.
TimelineBucket.title: TimelineBucket

UpdateCredentialRequest.description: Omitted fields stay unchanged; ``value`` rotates the secret.
UpdateCredentialRequest.title: UpdateCredentialRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description:
Omitted fields stay unchanged. ``display_name`` "" clears it;
``password`` resets it (revoking the user's sessions and tokens). The
username cannot be changed. An admin cannot disable, demote or reset
the password of their own account (409 OWN_ACCOUNT), and the last
active admin cannot be disabled or demoted (409 LAST_ADMIN).
UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest

UpdateWorkflowRequest.description:
Full replacement of name, description and draft (PUT semantics).

``expected_revision`` is the ``revision`` the client last read; a stale
value is rejected with 409 instead of overwriting newer work.
UpdateWorkflowRequest.title: UpdateWorkflowRequest

UserDetail.description: A user's public metadata: never a password hash, session or token.
UserDetail.title: UserDetail

ValidateWorkflowRequest.description: Optional: pin validation to the revision the client shows.
ValidateWorkflowRequest.title: ValidateWorkflowRequest

WorkflowFileOut.description: A workflow file's metadata; content travels in workflow packages only.
WorkflowFileOut.title: WorkflowFileOut

WorkflowRole.description: What a workflow's owner grants another user (workflow sharing).
WorkflowRole.title: WorkflowRole

WorkflowSort.description:
Workflow list orders; a leading ``-`` means descending. Every order
breaks ties by id, so pages are stable.
WorkflowSort.title: WorkflowSort

post.description: Change one's own password; other sessions are revoked.

get.description: The caller's session: who, and until when (absolute expiry).

Whether the first admin still has to be created (a fresh
installation); the UI then offers setup instead of sign-in.

post.description: Create the first admin; refused once any account exists.

get.description: The caller's personal access tokens (metadata only).

post.description:
Issue a personal access token for scripts and AI agents (bearer
token; acts with the caller's role). Needs the account password.
The token value is in this response only.

delete.description: Revoke one of the caller's tokens; it stops working at once.

post.description:
Accepted, not finished: the owning worker stops cooperatively at
its next heartbeat. A finished execution answers 409
INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION.

parameters.name: level

schema.description: Only lines at or above this level

parameters.description: Only lines whose message contains this text (case-insensitive)
parameters.name: q

schema.description: Only lines whose message contains this text (case-insensitive)
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: Window end, exclusive, with timezone; default now
parameters.name: until

schema.description: Window end, exclusive, with timezone; default now
schema.title: Until

post.description:
Every issue publish would find in one node's config, located for
form fields. Stateless: nothing is stored, and no value is echoed.

parameters.description: Remove even though workflows use it
parameters.name: force

schema.description: Remove even though workflows use it
schema.title: Force

post.description:
A new draft-only workflow with a copy of this workflow's draft (or
of published ``version``), owned by the caller.

get.description: The workflow package of published ``version``, or of the draft.
The owner, the members and the caller's own access.

delete.description: Stop sharing with a user; their next request is refused.

put.description:
Share the workflow with a user, or change their role. Takes effect
on their next request.

delete.description:
Stop being a member of a workflow shared with you; the owner
transfers ownership instead.

put.description:
Make another (enabled) user the owner. The previous owner stays
on as an editor. Answers the sharing as the caller now sees it.

post.description:
Replace the draft with a copy of ``version``; the version itself
stays as it is. Publishing the draft afterwards makes a new version.
